question: How much lighter is the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C than the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C?

Since we do not have the mass for the single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C, we can use the mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 350 °C (1.512) and the mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C (1.118) to estimate the mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C. 

Mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C = (1.512 - 1.118) / (350 - 400) * (400 - 350) + 1.118
Mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C = (0.394 / -50) * -50 + 1.118
Mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C = 0.394 + 1.118
Mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C = 1.512

Now we can find the difference in mass between the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C and the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C:
Difference in mass = Mass for single-layer standard group 2 at 400 °C - Mass for multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C
Difference in mass = 1.512 - 1.118
Difference in mass = 0.394
